question: A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

options.opd: The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) based on the clinical presentation and positive antinuclear antibodies. The initial treatment of choice for SLE with arthritis and pleuritis would be glucocorticoids at high doses to help control inflammation and disease activity.
